project_title: Graphic Novel Script Adapter Needed — Create Polished Sample for Crowdfunding

project_metadata.job_title: Graphic Novel Script Adapter Needed — Create Polished Sample for Crowdfunding
project_metadata.job_description:
I’m looking for a writer experienced in graphic novels, comics, or sequential storytelling to adapt a portion of my completed screenplay into a polished sample script for a future crowdfunding campaign.

This job is for a paid sample only (fixed price: $100). If the sample works well, there will be an opportunity to continue with the full graphic novel script.

What I need:

Adapt a selected section of my screenplay into a comic/graphic novel script format
Break the material into pages, panels, dialogue, captions, and visual direction
Maintain pacing, clarity, and strong visual storytelling
Deliver a clean, professional script sample suitable for showing to artists and potential backers

What I will provide:

The full screenplay
Character notes and tone/style references
The specific scene/sequence to adapt for the sample

Ideal experience:

Comic book or graphic novel writing
Screenplay adaptation
Panel‑by‑panel scripting
Storyboarding or sequential art familiarity (a plus)

This sample will be used to help pitch the project and secure funding. If we’re a good fit, there will be ongoing paid work as the project moves into full production.

Please include relevant writing samples, especially any comic or graphic novel work.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:
Hi [CLIENT_NAME_001].

Thanks for getting back to me so quickly. Let me address your questions.

1. My initial plan was to begin at the start and proceed as far into the story as possible. If you have a particular section you would rather have me concentrate on, though, I can focus there instead.

2. The sample folder I shared shows the script format I normally use. My recommendation is to lay out each page by panel. I occasionally indicate caption placement, but generally I leave the precise positioning of dialogue balloons and similar elements to the artist.

3. Because I would be adapting your script, my main influence over structure and pacing would come from determining how many panels, or how much room on the page, each moment receives. I expect those decisions to be reasonably clear on their own, but I can explain anything after drafting it if you want. Including explanatory notes would require additional time and would therefore raise my rate for the larger project.

I look forward to your reply.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: Excellent! Thanks for answering. I am continuing to assess all candidates today and expect to decide by my end of day (my time). If you have any questions, please let me know.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text:
Hello [FREELANCER_NAME_001],
I have one last question... how much time would you need to finish this sample project?
Thanks!
[CLIENT_NAME_002]

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:
Provided I can begin tomorrow, my target would be to return the script to you on Friday. That schedule would give me a little distance between the first and second draft while leaving room to address any questions that arise.
Thanks,
[FREELANCER_NAME_001]

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: I would like to proceed with the 12-page sample. If you want to accept, let me know and I will forward the contract. The terms will be those we discussed in our messages. Please ask if you have any questions; if not, I will send it shortly. Thanks!

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: I have attached additional files that should provide more information. Tell me if anything is unclear or if you need something further from me. I am available throughout the day and, if necessary, at night. Thanks!

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Excellent. It appears that you have already funded the project, so I will start working on it in the morning. I will contact you if any questions arise. Regardless, I will also try to send an update at the end of the day tomorrow.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:
A quick update: I made solid progress today and developed a preliminary breakdown that reaches Tom meeting Apollonia on comic page 12. I may ultimately find that this pacing is too quick if some beats require more room to breathe, but I will have to determine that while working.

I have two questions—or, more accurately, two possible approaches to the script that I would like to confirm with you:

1. In several spots, I am considering turning portions of the scene descriptions into "voice over" caption text.

2. To conserve page space and improve efficiency, I may omit a few brief exchanges. One example is at the bottom of page 23, when Carter tells Tom that he is invited to the dinner shown in the next scene.

I wanted to ask whether departures from the script on that scale are acceptable, or whether you want the comic to follow the screenplay line-for-line. Please let me know your preference.

Thanks.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text:
Hey [FREELANCER_NAME_001],
You have carte blanche on this. Because it is a sample piece, I will trust your judgement.
Tell me if you need anything from me.
[CLIENT_NAME_002]

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: One additional heads-up: I will be away from my desk during most of the day tomorrow. If you send any questions, I will respond as soon as I am able.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: Great work! I will contact you if anything further is needed. Let me know whether you are okay with leaving the contract open for a little longer. Thanks!

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Absolutely! There is no reason to close the job at this stage.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text:
Hello [FREELANCER_NAME_001]!
What would your total quote be for 80-85 pages?
Thanks!
[CLIENT_NAME_002]

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:
Hi! It's good to hear from you again.
Could you tell me how many episodes or screenplay pages you expect the 85 comic pages to encompass? Knowing that will help me estimate the required time.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: The original book was separated into 5 parts, and I am considering the first two parts for the first graphic novel. I can send you the files later this evening. I am finishing the production-cost calculations and plan to launch the crowdfunding on Monday, so I would appreciate receiving your quote before then. Thanks!

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Thank you. I will review the files already in my possession along with anything else you choose to send, then work through the calculations. I will try to provide the estimate this evening; if I cannot, I will send it on Sunday.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:
I ran some calculations using the material I have already written.

First, can you confirm whether you mean 85 screenplay pages or 85 comic pages? My adaptation came out to an approximate 2:1 ratio of screenplay pages to comic pages.

If part 2 is roughly equal in length to episode 1, then parts 1 and 2 should amount to approximately 40-45 comic pages. I could quote $350 for that scope with a timeline of 2 weeks. If I can reuse 12 pages from the sample script, possibly with light revisions and page reflowing, I could reduce the price to $275.

I can also produce 80-85 comic pages, but that would probably require covering more of the story, presumably through episode 3 or 4. For that amount of work, I would suggest $675 with a 4-week turnaround, or $600 even if the 12 sample-script pages can be reused.

Please tell me which option is nearer to what you have in mind and whether these terms work for you.

Thanks,
[FREELANCER_NAME_001]

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: The current projection is 85 pages of comic. Here are the next two scripts. I believe I also sent you a version of the novel, which is divided into three sections. That may serve as a better source than the scripts. Please review everything and tell me what you think.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: I am also setting aside a budget of $1500 for this service. Although I appreciate your quote, I believe that amount would compensate your time more appropriately. Let me know if you have any questions, and I will update you once I have news. Thanks!

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:
In that event, thank you very much. At that rate, I can devote additional time to determining the strongest presentation for all the material instead of adhering so closely to the screenplay.

Do you want me to begin next week, or should I wait until you explicitly tell me to "go?"

I can commit to writing 80-85 comic pages. I will review the next two episodes and the novel, then decide how much of the story can fit within that length. While planning it, should I pace the material with the expectation that I may eventually script the remainder of the story? In other words, should this portion feel self-contained, or should it be structured to leave readers wondering, "What's next?"

Thanks,
[FREELANCER_NAME_001]

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: I plan to post the listing on Monday. Would you object to my including your name as the project's scripter, or under whatever title you would prefer?

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:
I have no objection. My preferred credit is Corodon Fuller.

If you would rather avoid other bidders, you can create the next job as a follow-up to this one, or I can arrange it.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: I will create an additional milestone, but please keep in mind that I am counting on funding this through Kickstarter. Fingers crossed.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Just to confirm, is this portion of the job dependent on the Kickstarter receiving funding?

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: Yes. I thought I had made that clear. Does that affect whether you will be involved?

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:
I had understood that this work would help obtain crowdfunding, rather than that its own funding had not yet been secured.

Unfortunately, I cannot accept spec work through this site, and the job is too large for me to take on that basis even if it were permitted.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: I am sorry for the misunderstanding. I am hoping to obtain funding, and the sample I paid for was part of that effort. If the campaign succeeds, I will proceed with the project. I am not requesting any work from you at this time. However, if you prefer to withdraw, please tell me ASAP.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:
It is possible that I misunderstood, and I apologize if my response seemed abrupt. I will gladly proceed with the work after the funding is available, and I can postpone starting while you conduct the Kickstarter campaign.

Best of luck. I look forward to hearing that the campaign succeeded.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: No worries! I will send you the link once it is live. If you have a brief bio, I can include it in the listing, but that is entirely up to you.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text:
Here is the link. The pre-launch will happen tomorrow, followed by the full launch on Wednesday. You are welcome to share it.
[URL_001]

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: That's great. Thank you, and I hope it goes very well.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: Unfortunately, the outcome was not as positive as I had hoped. Thank you for your involvement and effort. I intend to close the contract tomorrow, and I will of course leave you a top-notch review. I appreciate the time you contributed.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: I am sorry the result was disappointing. Working with you has been a pleasure, and I wish you every success with your upcoming projects. If you need a writer in the future, please remember me.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text:
Hey [FREELANCER_NAME_001],
The artist assigned to this project has volunteered to produce additional artwork gratis and would like me to run the kickstarter again. If that is okay with you, I will therefore leave the contract open. I will let you know whenever the situation changes.
[CLIENT_NAME_002]

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: That's fine. Please tell me if there is anything further you need, and I will watch for updates.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text:
Hello [FREELANCER_NAME_001],
There is not much new to report right now. My current timeline is to launch this again by the end of July.
Thanks again for your help!
[CLIENT_NAME_002]

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: This project has now been placed on hold indefinitely, so I am going to close the contract. Thank you for your time; I will leave excellent feedback for you. If there is ever anything you need, please let me know.
